analysis.title: [GSX] Trade Idea: Not All Gloomy in Discretionary - Buy Consumer Experiences (GSXUCEXP Index)
key_insights: GS Consumer Experiences Basket (GSXUCEXP) has underperformed SPXXAI Index by 14%, even though spending growth on experiences accelerated from 1% in Q1 2025 to 6% in Q1 2026, versus 2% for broader services.
GS says the basket trades at attractive valuations, revisions appear close to inflecting, and positioning is not overly crowded.
Higher fuel costs have weighed on Consumer, the worst performing sector on GS's monitor YTD. GS says the basket's exposure to higher income cohorts has insulated it relative to the broader complex.
GS sees the basket as well positioned if oil prices stay elevated or in a potential de-escalation scenario.

The basket recently showed negative correlation with AI. GS expects the relationship to turn more positive as the value of experiences that cannot be replicated digitally rises, similar to the period after peak Metaverse enthusiasm in 2021.

Live Entertainment, Sports & Media (40% of basket): DIS reported 4% domestic per-capita spending growth, LYV more than 10% fan growth, MSGS record playoff gate revenues, and SPHR sold 3.6 million tickets generating $450mm from The Wizard of Oz.
Leisure & Theme Parks (20%): CHDN benefits from a flight to quality around the Kentucky Derby franchise, and OSW reported 14% growth in pre-booked wellness services.
Hotels & Travel (20%): MAR reported luxury RevPAR growth of more than 9% in the U.S. and Canada, H leisure transient RevPAR up 7%, HLT RevPAR up 3.9%.
Cruises (20%): CCL said bookings turned positive year-over-year in June and accelerated through July and August. VIK is 96% booked for 2026 with 2027 already 53% sold.

Earnings in Consumer Experiences have continued to move higher as prices have moved lower. Earnings revisions have lagged with rising oil prices but could inflect positive if earnings season brings momentum.
Ownership has rebounded from 2026 lows but remains below prior peaks. The median basket stock's relative valuation is low compared to the past decade.

Consumer Experiences stocks outperformed the discretionary sector over the last year. The recent pullback reflects oil costs and the health of US consumer spending. The basket began diverging from the Consumer Inertia Theme (GSXUSWCH) at the start of the year.

sector_views.rationale: GS recommends buying the Consumer Experiences basket on resilient experience spending, low relative valuation, near-inflecting revisions and non-crowded positioning, despite discretionary being the worst sector YTD on its monitor.

earnings_insights: GS expects earnings season to support positive revisions for the basket. The report is bullish 'ahead of earnings season' and cites company commentary (reported figures: DIS 4% domestic per-capita spending growth, LYV more than 10% fan growth, MAR luxury RevPAR above 9% US/Canada, H leisure transient RevPAR +7%, HLT RevPAR +3.9%, OSW 14% growth in pre-booked wellness services). These are company-reported operating metrics, not EPS or revenue figures.
CCL reported booking trends strengthening through the quarter, turning positive year-over-year in June. VIK is 96% booked for 2026 and 53% sold for 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Experience spending growth accelerated to 6% in Q1 2026 from 1% in Q1 2025. The basket has high-income exposure, low relative valuation, below-peak ownership and revisions that may inflect positive in earnings season.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher fuel costs have weighed on Consumer, the worst sector YTD on GS's monitor. Revisions have lagged with rising oil prices, and US consumer spending health is a concern.
